pathway.title: Terex Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has improved quickly but on a base that is not yet like-for-like. Net leverage fell from 4.59x at 2026-03-31 to 3.06x at 2026-09-30, with net debt of USD 2,171 million (3.01x and USD 2,138 million pro forma for the sale of two Specialty Vehicles businesses completed on 2026-10-23), but it was 2.89x at 2025-12-31 before REV, and the last-twelve-month earnings include REV only from 2026-02-02 with no pro forma EBITDA printed. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)

Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Company-stated liquidity was USD 1,207 million at 2026-09-30 with the USD 800 million revolver undrawn (pro forma cash after the October 2026 sale is not established), and the first principal maturity of size is the USD 600 million of 5% notes due in 2029, 23.1% of the principal ladder. The only maintenance covenant is tested above 30% revolver usage, a trigger of USD 240 million against a peak quarter-end drawing of USD 170 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F6; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47

Cash generation covers shareholder returns, but the merger consumed the cash. Free cash flow of USD 253 million in nine months 2026 was 47.4% of EBITDA (Reported), the unadjusted measure used for leverage, against 51.9% in FY2025 and 31.4% in FY2024. Dividends and buybacks took USD 133 million, leaving USD 120 million, yet net debt rose USD 359 million to USD 2,171 million (USD 2,138 million pro forma for the 2026-10-23 sale) because the REV cash price was USD 467 million. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48

Add-backs flatter Adjusted EBITDA and funding outside debt qualifies the leverage picture. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million for nine months includes USD 193 million of add-backs, 26.5% of the total, mostly deal costs and purchase accounting, so the leverage ratios here use the smaller EBITDA (Reported), which is conservative. Receivables sold of about USD 562 million, customer advances of USD 447 million, supplier finance of USD 51 million and repurchase and bond commitments of USD 460 million and USD 619 million sit outside debt, so a slowdown in orders or in factoring would reach liquidity before it reaches leverage. Basis: calculation F4; calculation F12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30

Margin stability is the weakest material dimension. Aerials earned a 5.4% Adjusted EBITDA margin on 30.0% of nine-month sales, its FY2025 segment operating margin fell 6.2 percentage points to 5.0% from 11.2%, and the Environmental Solutions margin fell to 17.0% from 19.8% on unfavourable mix, a utilities production ramp-up and lower refuse vehicle volumes, so the group Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 11.8% from 12.1% even with REV added. Basis: calculation F9; calculation F14; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 115–116; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 39–42

REV is now the largest earnings contributor and its integration is the central uncertainty, while the older businesses are well spread. Specialty Vehicles produced USD 262 million, 36.0% of group Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million, inside a purchase price allocation that is still provisional and with consumer recreational vehicles alongside public-service vehicles; management gives no REV synergy figure. Revenue is otherwise diversified, with no customer above 10% of sales and a USD 7.0 billion backlog at 2026-09-30. Basis: calculation F5; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18

Financial policy is the swing factor. Buybacks restarted in Q3 and up to USD 500 million more was authorised in October 2026, the 2.5x net leverage target of the FY2024 report is no longer stated, and legal limits on restricted payments were not supplied, so willingness to put debt reduction first cannot be shown; Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk as medium. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34

runs.text: Liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile are the strongest support. Company-stated liquidity of USD 1,207 million and an undrawn USD 800 million revolver mean a cyclical downturn would not force a refinancing before the USD 600 million of 5% notes fall due in 2029, which are 23.1% of the ladder, and the term loan and 2032 notes fall due later, so liquidity distress inside two years would need a sustained shock to earnings and cash flow, not a maturity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47

Cash generation covering distributions is the second strength. Free cash flow of USD 253 million exceeded dividends and buybacks of USD 133 million by USD 120 million in nine months 2026, so shareholder returns were covered by free cash flow on the evidence available, and the working capital ratio improved to 15.0% from 23.2%, which supports further cash release but could reverse. Basis: calculation F1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49

Product and customer diversification is the third strength. Four segments each carry 20.5% to 30.0% of nine-month sales, no customer exceeds 10%, and the backlog of USD 7.0 billion gives visibility for the enlarged group, so no single end market decides debt service. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18

A share-funded merger is the fourth strength. REV was paid 83.6% in shares, so the larger of the two acquisitions added little debt, and net debt moved by USD 359 million rather than the USD 3,384 million consideration. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F13

The first weakness is leverage on an unproven base. Net leverage of 3.06x (3.01x pro forma) sits above the 2.89x of 2025-12-31, includes REV earnings for only part of the period, and relies on EBITDA (Reported) because 26.5% of Adjusted EBITDA is add-backs, so lenders cannot yet test a like-for-like ratio. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F4

The second weakness is Aerials. At a 5.4% margin and 13.8% of group Adjusted EBITDA it cannot absorb a volume fall, and production cuts, unfavourable customer mix and tariffs cut its FY2025 operating margin by 6.2 percentage points, which makes group margin stability the weakest dimension. Basis: calculation F5; calculation F9; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42

The third weakness is dependence on REV. Specialty Vehicles supplies 36.0% of group Adjusted EBITDA inside provisional purchase accounting and brings customer advances and dealer repurchase commitments, so integration slippage would hit earnings and liquidity together. Basis: calculation F5; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

The fourth weakness is financial policy. Resumed buybacks, a new authorisation of up to USD 500 million and a leverage target that is no longer numeric weaken the anchor creditors can hold management to while legal limits are untested. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11

The fifth weakness is interest burden. EBITDA over interest expense fell to 3.54x in FY2025 from 6.80x in FY2024 and was 3.70x on a last-twelve-month basis, and the floating-rate term loan means each 100 bp adds about USD 12.27 million of interest before any hedge. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 29

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Two large acquisitions and several disposals have shaped the group since 2024. On 2024-10-08 Terex bought the Environmental Solutions Group from Dover Corporation for USD 2,010 million in cash, financed with USD 750 million of 6.25% senior notes due 2032 issued at par, a new USD 1,250 million term loan due 2031-10-08 and cash on hand; the revolver was enlarged to USD 800 million and extended to 2029-10-08 at the same time. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 26

On 2025-10-29 Terex agreed to acquire REV Group, Inc. in a stock-and-cash merger, which closed on 2026-02-02 with Terex taking 100% of REV's stock. Provisional consideration is USD 3,384 million in the 2026 reports and USD 3,262 million in the FY2025 annual report: USD 2,828 million in Terex shares valued at USD 58.99 each, USD 426 million of cash at USD 8.71 per REV share, USD 122 million of REV bank debt repaid at closing and USD 8 million for converted awards. REV added USD 1,744 million of net sales and USD 17 million of net income to 2026-09-30, goodwill of USD 1,428 million was assigned to Specialty Vehicles, and the purchase accounting remains provisional. Basis: calculation B5; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 21

The first-quarter 2026 cash flow shows the cash side of the REV deal: USD 467 million paid for acquisitions net of cash acquired, cash down from USD 772 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 392 million at 2026-03-31, and debt proceeds of USD 235 million against USD 70 million repaid, including a revolver drawing of USD 170 million that was undrawn again at 2026-09-30. No sentence names a funding source for the cash consideration. No new notes or term loan appear in the debt note at 2026-09-30 beyond those outstanding at 2025-12-31, so the 2024 financing for the Environmental Solutions Group is the latest new debt issue in the period; the term loan was repriced to SOFR plus 1.75% on 2025-08-12. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26

The tower and rough terrain crane businesses went to Raimondi Cranes SpA for USD 115 million (agreed 2025-08-06, closed 2025-10-31, pre-tax gain USD 41 million). Capacity of Texas, Inc. and Mobile Products, Inc. (LayMor), two Specialty Vehicles businesses, were held for sale at 2026-09-30 with a non-cash loss of USD 20 million and were sold on 2026-10-23 to Right Lane Industries for about USD 33 million, a subsequent event that is not in the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. A further sale of an unnamed Specialty Vehicles business in the first quarter of 2026 appears only in the reconciliation notes, with no buyer or price. A strategic review of Aerials, announced with the REV merger, has no reported outcome. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 36

After quarter end the Board authorised repurchases of up to USD 500 million more in October 2026 and declared a dividend of USD 0.17 per share payable on 2026-12-18 to holders of record on 2026-11-09. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source readiness for Terex Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the five supplied Terex filings can support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, and what they leave out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document date is the date the registrant signed the report; the reports do not state a filing date. No earlier-module output is supplied to Source readiness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied Terex filings support a credit snapshot as of 2026-09-30, with limits: the REV merger of February 2026 breaks comparability with earlier periods, so creditors should not read year-on-year or LTM figures across it as like-for-like.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 407 million, total debt of USD 2,578 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 800 million are printed for that date. Covenant headroom, LTM Adjusted EBITDA, ratings, market prices and anything dated after 2026-10-29 are not established from the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The group a lender faces today is larger and different from the one the audited annual report describes. The REV merger closed on 2026-02-02 and created a fourth segment, Specialty Vehicles. REV contributed net sales of USD 1,744 million and net income of USD 17 million from the closing date to 2026-09-30. Unaudited pro forma figures are printed only for net sales, net income and earnings per share, so no combined EBITDA or leverage can be taken from the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two reporting differences matter more than their size suggests. From 2026-01-01 the company shows amortisation of customer relationships and trade names as an operating expense instead of cost of goods sold, and it recast only the 2025 quarterly comparatives, by USD 52 million for the first nine months; the audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements print no separate amortisation line, so gross profit and the operating expense lines do not line up across the two kinds of filing while operating profit does. The REV purchase price is also printed twice, USD 3,262 million in the annual report and USD 3,384 million in the quarterly reports, and the gap equals the USD 122 million of REV debt repaid at closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 137; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt and liquidity are well documented at the latest date. Three funded instruments remain: senior notes due 2029, senior notes due 2032 and a term loan due 2031, with the USD 800 million revolver, drawn USD 170 million at 2026-03-31 and USD 110 million at 2026-06-30, undrawn at 2026-09-30 and expiring on 2029-10-08. The only maintenance covenant is a first lien net leverage test of 3.00x on the revolver, applied only when more than 30% of it is used; the company says it complies but prints no ratio, and the credit agreement itself was not supplied. The 2024 annual report stated a 2.5x net leverage target through the cycle; the 2025 annual report drops the number.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 24–27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are only partly refreshed. The latest operating lease liabilities, USD 129 million, are dated 2025-12-31 before the merger, and the latest pension funded status is dated 2024-12-31. The 2026 reports add repurchase commitments with a maximum contingent liability of USD 460 million, performance, bid and specialty bonds of USD 619 million, short-term customer advances of USD 271 million, long-term customer advances of USD 176 million and receivable sales of about USD 562 million in the first nine months; none of these is inside the debt figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA exists only in the 2026 quarterly reports: USD 727 million for the first nine months of 2026 against USD 495 million for the same months of 2025. The annual reports print no EBITDA reconciliation, so a twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA to 2026-09-30 cannot be built from the supplied documents, and it would blend pre-merger and post-merger perimeters. The 2025 annual report does print operating profit for each 2025 quarter, including USD 137 million for the fourth quarter, and a 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA that includes REV from closing and is not updated in the 2026 reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the quarter end the third-quarter report prints three events: completion on 2026-10-23 of the sale of two Specialty Vehicles businesses for about USD 33 million, a further share repurchase authorisation of up to USD 500 million in October 2026, and a USD 0.17 per share dividend payable on 2026-12-18. The latest document is dated 2026-10-29, so the period to the as-of date of 2026-11-18 is not covered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a ready-with-limits view is that the combined business has three quarters of history, a provisional purchase price allocation and no pro forma EBITDA, which could make any leverage reading of the new group unreliable. The filings point the other way on two counts: the company recasts its 2025 quarters and discloses REV’s own contribution, and the REV goodwill estimate rose by USD 19 million in the second quarter and fell by USD 42 million in the third, from USD 1,451 million at the first quarter to USD 1,428 million at the third.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The executed credit agreement and indentures would turn the covenant and guarantor statements into testable terms, and a FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation or REV’s own annual report would allow a leverage measure on one perimeter. A larger revision of the REV accounting, or a revolver draw above 30%, would raise the weight of the covenant gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This view concerns what the filings contain and where, not credit quality: it makes no leverage, coverage or recovery judgement, and the arithmetic it carries ties printed figures to their printed parts. Page references point to positions in the supplied text files, which flatten tables into lines, so each figure was read against its row label; they are not the filings’ printed page numbers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 reports are unaudited and the REV accounting stays provisional until its measurement period closes, so figures that depend on it can still change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row ties a figure used above to its printed parts; none is an analytical result.

fields.value: Five differences limit comparison. Full-year EBITDA is calculated because the annual reports print none, so last-twelve-month figures mix a calculated year with printed interim figures. Debt at 2025-12-31 is USD 2,584 million on the balance sheet, USD 2,592 million as principal and USD 2,552 million under a line labelled net debt, and the first is used. The 2026 quarterly reports move amortisation of customer relationships and trade names out of cost of goods sold, so gross profit is not comparable with the annual reports, while operating profit is. The REV purchase price is USD 3,262 million in the annual report and USD 3,384 million in the quarterly reports, and letters of credit at 2025-12-31 are USD 85 million in one set of filings and USD 50 million in another.

fields.value: The strongest case that leverage is better than 3.06x is that REV earnings are only partly in the base: nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million exceeds EBITDA (Reported) of USD 534 million by USD 193 million of add-backs, mainly deal-related and purchase accounting items, and pro forma net sales for the nine months were USD 6,359 million against reported USD 6,169 million. The case that it is worse is that those add-backs are large and their realisation status is not stated, that FY2025 EBITDA of USD 626 million is calculated and cannot be tested against an issuer figure, and that cash interest paid is not available to test cover for 2026. A printed FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, a pro forma EBITDA for REV or quarterly cash interest paid would settle the point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Terex Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: what Terex does and where it earns, who owns and controls it, the acquisitions and disposals that reshaped it, and the governance and capital-allocation behaviour that bears on creditors, taken from the five supplied filings and the source-readiness summary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document date is the date the registrant signed the report; the reports do not state a filing date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Terex's creditor risk lies in management's financial policy, not in a controlling owner: no controlling shareholder is disclosed, yet two large acquisitions since October 2024 and a new USD 500 million buyback authorisation test that policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors are protected by funding mix and diversification: 83.6% of the REV consideration was paid in shares, no customer exceeds 10% of sales and the largest is below 6%. They remain exposed to an unresolved review of Aerials, which is 30.0% of nine-month 2026 sales, and to buybacks that resumed in Q3 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling owner is disclosed in the supplied filings, so creditors face a public-company board and management rather than a sponsor, and the usual tests of sponsor support or extraction do not apply. The REV merger gave former REV holders shares equal to 42.1% of those outstanding on 2026-02-10. No block holder is named in the supplied filings, and holders above 5%, board independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B6; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is more diversified by product and customer than by region, and REV has made it more North American. Four segments each carry 20.5% to 30.0% of nine-month 2026 net sales, no customer exceeds 10% and the largest is below 6%, yet North America produced 81.1% of nine-month 2026 sales against 72.3% in FY2025. The customer figures predate REV.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B4; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Aerials is the weak earner and the asset under review. It supplies 30.0% of nine-month 2026 sales but only 12.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, at a 5.4% margin against 15.0% to 17.8% elsewhere, and its Adjusted EBITDA fell USD 31 million year on year, which the company attributes to tariff costs, unfavourable mix and inflation. Without Aerials the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin would be 14.5% against 11.8%, before any reallocation of corporate costs, but a sale would also remove the largest sales base, and no timetable, price or use of proceeds has been disclosed a year after the review was announced alongside the REV merger.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 52

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The two acquisitions were funded very differently, and REV was the more creditor-friendly one on funding mix. The Environmental Solutions Group cost USD 2,010 million in cash and was financed with USD 2,000 million of new notes and term loan plus cash on hand, while 83.6% of the REV consideration was paid in shares and the cash element was USD 548 million, including USD 122 million of REV bank debt repaid at closing. The first-quarter 2026 cash flow shows cash falling and new borrowing, but no sentence names the source of that cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B7; calculation B5; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are resuming while the REV purchase accounting is still provisional. Nine-month 2026 dividends of USD 58 million and buybacks of USD 75 million took 52.6% of free cash flow of USD 253 million, buybacks restarted in Q3 after none in the first half, and an October 2026 authorisation of up to USD 500 million lifts repurchase capacity to USD 610.8 million. The debt agreements restrict dividends, but their limits were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B8; calculation B9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and reporting are conventional and clean on the evidence available, but untestable for creditor protections. The chairman is non-executive and separate from the chief executive, the auditor gave unqualified opinions on the FY2025 statements and internal control with one critical audit matter on inventory quantities in Aerials and Materials Processing, and the 2026 reports add REV controls from closing. Related-party dealings, director independence, pay and the executed debt documents were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 52; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's claims on REV are not yet evidence. The second-quarter report says integration is progressing as planned and the FY2025 report says ESG integration is complete and ahead of its USD 25 million synergy commitment, but no REV synergy figure is given, the 2.5x net leverage target of the FY2024 report is no longer stated, and the 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA predates three quarters of results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall governance and financial-policy risk is medium. The supplied filings show no extraction, related-party payment or creditor-adverse transaction and a mostly share-funded merger, set against debt-funded growth in 2024, resumed buybacks, an open portfolio review and legal limits that cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B5; calculation B7; calculation B8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a more positive view is that the REV merger was paid mostly in shares, the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30, no single customer dominates and no distribution is shown to have been debt-funded. Management also reports Q3 free cash flow of USD 209 million and a backlog of USD 7.0 billion, and the auditor found internal control effective at 2025-12-31. On that evidence the risk could be judged low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if the executed credit agreement shows wide capacity for restricted payments, if buybacks are funded from revolver drawings or run ahead of free cash flow, if proceeds of an Aerials sale go to shareholders rather than to debt, or if the REV purchase accounting moves materially again. It would improve if the company restates a numeric leverage target, commits sale proceeds to debt reduction or discloses covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two large acquisitions and several disposals have shaped the group since 2024. On 2024-10-08 Terex bought the Environmental Solutions Group from Dover Corporation for USD 2,010 million in cash, financed with USD 750 million of 6.25% senior notes due 2032 issued at par, a new USD 1,250 million term loan due 2031-10-08 and cash on hand; the revolver was enlarged to USD 800 million and extended to 2029-10-08 at the same time.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2025-10-29 Terex agreed to acquire REV Group, Inc. in a stock-and-cash merger, which closed on 2026-02-02 with Terex taking 100% of REV's stock. Provisional consideration is USD 3,384 million in the 2026 reports and USD 3,262 million in the FY2025 annual report: USD 2,828 million in Terex shares valued at USD 58.99 each, USD 426 million of cash at USD 8.71 per REV share, USD 122 million of REV bank debt repaid at closing and USD 8 million for converted awards. REV added USD 1,744 million of net sales and USD 17 million of net income to 2026-09-30, goodwill of USD 1,428 million was assigned to Specialty Vehicles, and the purchase accounting remains provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B5; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first-quarter 2026 cash flow shows the cash side of the REV deal: USD 467 million paid for acquisitions net of cash acquired, cash down from USD 772 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 392 million at 2026-03-31, and debt proceeds of USD 235 million against USD 70 million repaid, including a revolver drawing of USD 170 million that was undrawn again at 2026-09-30. No sentence names a funding source for the cash consideration. No new notes or term loan appear in the debt note at 2026-09-30 beyond those outstanding at 2025-12-31, so the 2024 financing for the Environmental Solutions Group is the latest new debt issue in the period; the term loan was repriced to SOFR plus 1.75% on 2025-08-12.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The tower and rough terrain crane businesses went to Raimondi Cranes SpA for USD 115 million (agreed 2025-08-06, closed 2025-10-31, pre-tax gain USD 41 million). Capacity of Texas, Inc. and Mobile Products, Inc. (LayMor), two Specialty Vehicles businesses, were held for sale at 2026-09-30 with a non-cash loss of USD 20 million and were sold on 2026-10-23 to Right Lane Industries for about USD 33 million, a subsequent event that is not in the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. A further sale of an unnamed Specialty Vehicles business in the first quarter of 2026 appears only in the reconciliation notes, with no buyer or price. A strategic review of Aerials, announced with the REV merger, has no reported outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Terex Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall credit profile, its strongest support and its primary downside, built from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance answers; no rating, relative value, legal or sizing view is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document date is the date the registrant signed the report; the reports do not state a filing date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Terex's fundamental credit is adequate but unproven: net leverage eased to 3.06x at 2026-09-30 (3.01x pro forma for the sale completed on 2026-10-23) and liquidity is USD 1,207 million, yet REV earnings are only partly in the ratio and Aerials margins are weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No significant debt maturities until 2029 protect creditors from a refinancing squeeze. The primary downside path is a cyclical fall in rental and infrastructure demand that compresses Aerials and equipment margins while REV integration is still unproven, pushing leverage back toward the 4.59x seen at 2026-03-31. Free cash flow of USD 253 million in nine months covered USD 133 million of shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has improved quickly but on a base that is not yet like-for-like. Net leverage fell from 4.59x at 2026-03-31 to 3.06x at 2026-09-30, with net debt of USD 2,171 million (3.01x and USD 2,138 million pro forma for the sale of two Specialty Vehicles businesses completed on 2026-10-23), but it was 2.89x at 2025-12-31 before REV, and the last-twelve-month earnings include REV only from 2026-02-02 with no pro forma EBITDA printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Company-stated liquidity was USD 1,207 million at 2026-09-30 with the USD 800 million revolver undrawn (pro forma cash after the October 2026 sale is not established), and the first principal maturity of size is the USD 600 million of 5% notes due in 2029, 23.1% of the principal ladder. The only maintenance covenant is tested above 30% revolver usage, a trigger of USD 240 million against a peak quarter-end drawing of USD 170 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F6; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation covers shareholder returns, but the merger consumed the cash. Free cash flow of USD 253 million in nine months 2026 was 47.4% of EBITDA (Reported), the unadjusted measure used for leverage, against 51.9% in FY2025 and 31.4% in FY2024. Dividends and buybacks took USD 133 million, leaving USD 120 million, yet net debt rose USD 359 million to USD 2,171 million (USD 2,138 million pro forma for the 2026-10-23 sale) because the REV cash price was USD 467 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Add-backs flatter Adjusted EBITDA and funding outside debt qualifies the leverage picture. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million for nine months includes USD 193 million of add-backs, 26.5% of the total, mostly deal costs and purchase accounting, so the leverage ratios here use the smaller EBITDA (Reported), which is conservative. Receivables sold of about USD 562 million, customer advances of USD 447 million, supplier finance of USD 51 million and repurchase and bond commitments of USD 460 million and USD 619 million sit outside debt, so a slowdown in orders or in factoring would reach liquidity before it reaches leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F4; calculation F12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability is the weakest material dimension. Aerials earned a 5.4% Adjusted EBITDA margin on 30.0% of nine-month sales, its FY2025 segment operating margin fell 6.2 percentage points to 5.0% from 11.2%, and the Environmental Solutions margin fell to 17.0% from 19.8% on unfavourable mix, a utilities production ramp-up and lower refuse vehicle volumes, so the group Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 11.8% from 12.1% even with REV added.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F9; calculation F14; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 115–116; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 39–42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: REV is now the largest earnings contributor and its integration is the central uncertainty, while the older businesses are well spread. Specialty Vehicles produced USD 262 million, 36.0% of group Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million, inside a purchase price allocation that is still provisional and with consumer recreational vehicles alongside public-service vehicles; management gives no REV synergy figure. Revenue is otherwise diversified, with no customer above 10% of sales and a USD 7.0 billion backlog at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F5; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor. Buybacks restarted in Q3 and up to USD 500 million more was authorised in October 2026, the 2.5x net leverage target of the FY2024 report is no longer stated, and legal limits on restricted payments were not supplied, so willingness to put debt reduction first cannot be shown; Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk as medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a more positive view is that leverage may already be lower than 3.06x: the last-twelve-month base holds REV for about eight of twelve months, Adjusted EBITDA was USD 286 million in Q3 2026 against USD 186 million a year earlier, and the 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA, if met, would exceed the USD 710 million of EBITDA (Reported) in the ratio. With USD 1,207 million of liquidity and no maturities until 2029, the profile could then be judged strong on cash flow. The outlook dates from 2026-02-13 and has not been updated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would weaken if net leverage on the enlarged perimeter stays near 3.06x once a full twelve months of REV is in the base, if the Aerials margin falls below 5.4%, if buybacks outrun free cash flow or if revolver usage approaches the USD 240 million test trigger. It would strengthen if the company prints pro forma EBITDA that confirms leverage near 3x, restates a numeric leverage target or applies Aerials sale proceeds to debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F6; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No pro forma EBITDA is printed for the enlarged group, so the adequate-but-unproven view could move either way once REV earnings are shown for a full twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, market price or peer figure was supplied, so standing against sector issuers and market access are not established and the refinancing judgement rests on the maturity profile and liquidity alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the covenant definitions, restricted-payment room and guarantor perimeter behind the liquidity conclusion are unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sector view rests on management statements about end-market demand, with no independent industry data, so the outlook for rental, waste, utility and emergency-vehicle demand is management language only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The financial profile uses calculated full-year EBITDA and interim figures printed by the company, so cash conversion ratios compare periods only as labelled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile are the strongest support. Company-stated liquidity of USD 1,207 million and an undrawn USD 800 million revolver mean a cyclical downturn would not force a refinancing before the USD 600 million of 5% notes fall due in 2029, which are 23.1% of the ladder, and the term loan and 2032 notes fall due later, so liquidity distress inside two years would need a sustained shock to earnings and cash flow, not a maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation covering distributions is the second strength. Free cash flow of USD 253 million exceeded dividends and buybacks of USD 133 million by USD 120 million in nine months 2026, so shareholder returns were covered by free cash flow on the evidence available, and the working capital ratio improved to 15.0% from 23.2%, which supports further cash release but could reverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Product and customer diversification is the third strength. Four segments each carry 20.5% to 30.0% of nine-month sales, no customer exceeds 10%, and the backlog of USD 7.0 billion gives visibility for the enlarged group, so no single end market decides debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A share-funded merger is the fourth strength. REV was paid 83.6% in shares, so the larger of the two acquisitions added little debt, and net debt moved by USD 359 million rather than the USD 3,384 million consideration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is leverage on an unproven base. Net leverage of 3.06x (3.01x pro forma) sits above the 2.89x of 2025-12-31, includes REV earnings for only part of the period, and relies on EBITDA (Reported) because 26.5% of Adjusted EBITDA is add-backs, so lenders cannot yet test a like-for-like ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is Aerials. At a 5.4% margin and 13.8% of group Adjusted EBITDA it cannot absorb a volume fall, and production cuts, unfavourable customer mix and tariffs cut its FY2025 operating margin by 6.2 percentage points, which makes group margin stability the weakest dimension.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F5; calculation F9; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is dependence on REV. Specialty Vehicles supplies 36.0% of group Adjusted EBITDA inside provisional purchase accounting and brings customer advances and dealer repurchase commitments, so integration slippage would hit earnings and liquidity together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F5; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is financial policy. Resumed buybacks, a new authorisation of up to USD 500 million and a leverage target that is no longer numeric weaken the anchor creditors can hold management to while legal limits are untested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is interest burden. EBITDA over interest expense fell to 3.54x in FY2025 from 6.80x in FY2024 and was 3.70x on a last-twelve-month basis, and the floating-rate term loan means each 100 bp adds about USD 12.27 million of interest before any hedge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status is Ready with Limitations. All five filings, Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance are in the run for 2026-11-18 and agree on the entity, the 2026-09-30 balance sheet date and the REV perimeter break, but no ratings, market prices, peer data, executed debt documents or pro forma EBITDA were supplied. The datapoints used from Financial foundation are net debt of USD 2,171 million (USD 2,138 million pro forma for the 2026-10-23 sale), net leverage of 3.06x (3.01x pro forma), liquidity of USD 1,207 million and EBITDA (Reported) of USD 710 million for the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Terex makes capital equipment in four segments: Environmental Solutions (refuse bodies, utility equipment), Materials Processing (crushing, screening, material handling), Specialty Vehicles (fire and ambulance vehicles, terminal trucks, recreational vehicles, from REV) and Aerials (aerial work platforms, telehandlers). Equipment is sold through distributors, rental companies and direct sales, so cash flow follows customer capital spending, and the installed base supports parts and service whose share of revenue is not printed. The acquisitions of the Environmental Solutions Group in October 2024 and REV in February 2026 moved the mix toward waste, utilities and emergency vehicles that management describes as less cyclical, which supports cash-flow visibility if the claim holds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Terex is listed, with no controlling holder named in the supplied filings, so there is no sponsor whose support or extraction must be judged; creditors depend on a board with a non-executive chairman and on the debt documents, which were not supplied. Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk as medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and project-driven: in 2025 Aerials sales fell 14.5% on weaker demand from independent rental customers exposed to smaller, rate-sensitive projects, and Materials Processing sales fell 11.6% on macro uncertainty, high interest rates and weak European demand, while national customers and large projects drove the 2026 recovery in Aerials. The mechanism is that rental and dealer customers defer fleet purchases when rates are high, which cuts volumes and absorption; the implication is that revenue durability is average, supported by replacement demand in waste, utilities and emergency vehicles that management calls stable but that is only management language. Price-cost discipline is cited in Materials Processing, and no pass-through figure is printed, so pricing power is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are the weakest dimension. Group Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.8% for nine months 2026 against 12.1%, operating margin fell to 4.7% from 8.2% mainly on purchase accounting, and Aerials earned 5.4%, so a volume fall with under-absorbed plants would hit Aerials first. Management cites cost-out actions, a plant closure in Aerials and the Terex Operating System, and gross profit margin was 17.6% for nine months 2026 against 20.8% on mix and the REV addition, but fixed versus variable cost is not split in the filings, so operating leverage cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low: capital expenditure was USD 90 million in nine months 2026 and USD 118 million in FY2025, so most EBITDA can reach cash, and conversion to free cash flow was 31.4%, 51.9% and 47.4% of EBITDA (Reported) in FY2024, FY2025 and nine months 2026. The 2025 and 2026 figures were helped by a working capital release, from 24.0% of sales at 2024-12-31 to 20.8% a year later and 15.0% at 2026-09-30, and by about USD 562 million of receivables sold in nine months 2026, so a reversal would cut cash conversion; capex is the main lever, with dividends and buybacks of USD 133 million the next. REV transaction costs of USD 19 million in nine months 2026 are another claim on cash, and cash interest paid is not printed for 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and varies by product: the company names no single competitor across segments, and in Aerials the primary competitors named include Oshkosh (JLG), Haulotte, JCB, Manitou and Dingli, which limits price increases and exposes margin to tariffs. Buyer power is high because national rental companies buy a material part of Aerials and Environmental Solutions output and customer consolidation increases pricing pressure, while supplier consolidation limits sources for some parts. Substitution risk and the threat of new entry are not established from the filings, so the credit effect is margin pressure from the largest buyers rather than a loss of volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariffs and interest rates are material. Higher tariff costs cut Aerials nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, USD 40 million of tariff refunds were recognised in nine months 2026 and further claims await customs review, and high interest rates weigh on rent-to-own conversions and smaller projects, so policy shifts move margins and fleet purchases. Government infrastructure funding and municipal budgets support Aerials, Materials Processing and emergency vehicles, which is management's view only. Other social and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the supplied materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are USD 1,207 million of liquidity, distant maturities, share-funded REV consideration and low capital intensity, which keep debt service secure through a mid-cycle slowdown. Weaknesses are leverage on an unproven base, Aerials margin and dependence on REV, which cap the profile at adequate. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are demonstrated REV synergies, an Aerials sale applied to debt and continued working capital release. Threats are a rental and infrastructure downturn, tariffs, resumed buybacks and a customer-advance reversal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F5; calculation F7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: net sales of USD 7,487 million over the last twelve months give shock absorption, but no market share is printed. Competitive advantage is average, with brands and distribution but no evidence of pricing power. Business diversification is average, strong by product and customer but with 81.1% of nine-month sales in North America. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with low capex but unsplit fixed costs. Margin stability is weak, as set out above. Free cash flow stability is average, positive in each period but dependent on working capital and receivable sales. Ability to refinance is average, with no maturities until 2029 but no ratings or market data. Liquidity is strong at USD 1,207 million. Financial policy and governance is average, with medium risk in Business & governance. The trend is improving leverage on a larger base, constrained by add-backs, tariffs and the missing pro forma EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F3; calculation F5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the outlook rests on REV integration, tariffs and the Aerials review. Management's 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA implies USD 203 million to USD 273 million in the fourth quarter if it uses the Adjusted EBITDA basis, against USD 286 million in Q3, a gap that suggests the outlook is cautious or out of date, and it was not updated. Tailwinds are a USD 7.0 billion backlog, replacement demand and utility grid investment, which support revenue and deleveraging. Headwinds are tariffs, rental customers managing capital spending and absorbing delivered fleets, and higher interest on the floating term loan. Over three to five years the filings give no guidance; the structural sector tailwinds are management's view, so the medium-term view is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F10; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a cyclical fall in rental-company fleet purchases and infrastructure projects, as happened to Aerials in 2025 when sales fell 14.5% and production was cut. The first operational break is under-absorption and lower shipments in Aerials, Materials Processing and refuse bodies, followed by weaker orders at Specialty Vehicles and slower customer advances. Financial transmission is a lower EBITDA with margins already thin in Aerials, a working capital build that reverses the release, and less room from receivable sales; a fall of 33.4% in last-twelve-month EBITDA (Reported) would return net leverage to the 4.59x seen in March 2026 (reported net debt is used), and a smaller fall would leave it between 3.06x and 4.59x, the range of pressure this scenario implies. Liquidity would still be supported by cash and the revolver, whose test applies only above USD 240 million of drawings against a peak of USD 170 million, and no maturity falls before 2029. Management levers are suspending buybacks and dividends (USD 133 million in nine months 2026), low capex, working capital release, restructuring in Aerials and the Aerials sale. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, with the credit effect showing as leverage and margin pressure. Observable triggers are falling backlog, Aerials margin below 5.4%, revolver usage rising and buybacks above free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F6; calculation F11; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Terex presents an adequate business profile supported by USD 1,207 million of liquidity, product and customer diversification and a share-funded REV merger, but credit quality is constrained by leverage on an unproven earnings base, weak Aerials margins and resumed shareholder returns. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covered returns by USD 120 million yet depends on working capital and receivable sales. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on REV delivering earnings before the USD 600 million of 2029 notes approach maturity and on the Aerials outcome. The primary downside path is a rental and infrastructure downturn that compresses Aerials and group margins while REV is bedding in. Business profile against typical sector issuers is not established because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, the executed debt documents, ratings and the Aerials outcome. Top risk: leverage rising again on an unproven earnings base.
